manifest_changes.heading: Statement
manifest_changes.before: For independent centered real variables bounded by b with total variance V>0, each one-sided tail at t>0 is at most exp(-t^2/(2(V+bt/3))); if V=0 their sum vanishes almost surely.
manifest_changes.after:
Let $Z_1,\ldots,Z_m$ be independent, integrable, centered real random variables on a probability space, with $|Z_i|\le b$ almost surely for a finite $b>0$. Put $S_m=\sum_{i=1}^mZ_i$ and $V=\sum_{i=1}^m\mathbb E[Z_i^2]$. For every $t>0$, if $V>0$ then
$$\mathbb P(S_m\ge t)\le\exp\!\left(-\frac{t^2}{2(V+bt/3)}\right),\qquad \mathbb P(S_m\le-t)\le\exp\!\left(-\frac{t^2}{2(V+bt/3)}\right).$$
If $V=0$, then $S_m=0$ almost surely.

manifest_changes.heading: Remarks
manifest_changes.before: The normalized-gamma existence theorem and finite-partition update state no topology or density model. Weak support needs a topology and positive prior neighborhood mass; density-posterior consistency or contraction additionally needs a specified sampling model, truth class and its own proof under the relevant hypotheses.
manifest_changes.after:
The normalized-gamma construction and finite-partition posterior update
state no topology on $\mathcal P(\mathsf X)$ and specify no density model.
They therefore establish neither a weak-support theorem nor density-posterior
consistency or contraction. A weak-support claim requires a specified topology
and an argument that the prior assigns positive mass to each neighborhood in
question. A density-posterior consistency or contraction claim additionally
requires a specified sampling model and truth class, plus its own proof under
the relevant model-specific hypotheses. For example, the finite-dimensional
prior-mass bound in Ghosal--van der Vaart is one ingredient in a separate
mixture analysis, not a consequence of the conjugate update alone.

manifest_changes.heading: Statement
manifest_changes.after:
Let $\mathcal P(\mathbb R)$ be the probability measures on the Borel sets of
$\mathbb R$, equipped with the evaluation sigma-algebra, and let $\sigma>0$.
For $F\in\mathcal P(\mathbb R)$ define
$$p_{F,\sigma}(x):=\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{1}{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}}\exp\!\left(-\frac{(x-z)^2}{2\sigma^2}\right)F(dz).$$
Then $(F,\sigma,x)\mapsto p_{F,\sigma}(x)$ is jointly measurable,
$0<p_{F,\sigma}(x)\le(\sigma\sqrt{2\pi})^{-1}$ for every $(F,\sigma,x)$,
and $\int_{\mathbb R}p_{F,\sigma}(x)\,dx=1$. In particular it is the
Lebesgue density of the convolution of $F$ with $N(0,\sigma^2)$.

manifest_changes.heading: Statement
manifest_changes.after:
There is a universal constant $C$ such that, for $A,\sigma>0$,
$0<\eta<1/2$, and every probability measure $F$ supported on $[-A,A]$,
there is a discrete probability measure $F'$ on $[-A,A]$ with at most
$$C(A/\sigma\vee1)\log(e/\eta)$$
support points and
$$\|p_{F,\sigma}-p_{F',\sigma}\|_1\le\eta,\qquad \|p_{F,\sigma}-p_{F',\sigma}\|_\infty\le\eta/\sigma.$$

manifest_changes.heading: Statement
manifest_changes.before:
Assume AC. Let $p_0\in C^2(\mathbb R)$ be a probability density with compact support $K$, a finite union of intervals. Suppose $J=\int_{\{p_0>0\}}(p_0'')^2/p_0<\infty$ and there are $a,c>0$ such that $P_0(I)\ge c\lambda(I)^a$ for every interval $I\subseteq K$. Let $F\sim DP(\alpha)$, where $\alpha$ is a finite nonzero measure with continuous strictly positive density on a neighborhood of $K$, and independently let $S\sim G$ for any probability measure $G$ on $(0,\infty)$. Suppose $n^{-a_1}\lesssim\sigma_n\lesssim n^{-a_2}$ for $0<a_2<a_1<1$, and put $\sigma=\sigma_nS$. Then for constants $C_1,C_2>0$ and all sufficiently large $n$,
$$\Pi_n\left\{\mathrm{KL}(P_0\Vert P_{F,\sigma})\le C_1\sigma_n^4,\quad P_0\left[\log\frac{p_0}{p_{F,\sigma}}\right]^2\le C_1\sigma_n^4\right\}\ge\exp\{-C_2\sigma_n^{-1}(\log n)^2\}.$$
Consequently, for $d_n=\max\{(n\sigma_n)^{-1/2}\log n,\sigma_n^2\}$, the same two local quantities are at most $C_1d_n^2$ on a set of prior mass at least $e^{-C_3nd_n^2}$. Logarithmic integrands vanish where $p_0=0$.
manifest_changes.after:

Suppose $J=\int_{\{p_0>0\}}(p_0'')^2/p_0<\infty$ and there are $a,c>0$ such that $P_0(I)\ge c\lambda(I)^a$ for every interval $I\subseteq K$. Suppose $n^{-a_1}\lesssim\sigma_n\lesssim n^{-a_2}$ for $0<a_2<a_1<1$, and put $\sigma=\sigma_nS$. Then for constants $C_1,C_2>0$ and all sufficiently large $n$,

manifest_changes.heading: Statement
manifest_changes.before:
Assume AC. Let $p\in C^2(\mathbb R)$ be a nonnegative compactly supported probability density and suppose
$$J:=\int_{\{p>0\}}\frac{(p''(x))^2}{p(x)}\,dx<\infty.$$
For $\sigma>0$, set $q_\sigma=p*\phi_\sigma$, where $\phi_\sigma$ is the centered normal density with standard deviation $\sigma$. Then
$$\int\frac{(p-q_\sigma)^2}{q_\sigma}\,dx\le\frac49\sigma^4J,\qquad \mathrm{KL}(p\Vert q_\sigma)\le\frac49\sigma^4J,\qquad \int p\left[\log\frac p{q_\sigma}\right]^2dx\le\frac49\sigma^4J.$$
The logarithmic integrands are zero where $p=0$. No unimodality or uniform bound on $p/q_\sigma$ is assumed.
manifest_changes.after:
Assume AC. Let $p\in C^2(\mathbb R)$ be a nonnegative compactly supported probability density and suppose
$$J:=\int_{\{p>0\}}\frac{(p''(x))^2}{p(x)}\,dx<\infty.$$
For $\sigma>0$, set $q_\sigma=p*\phi_\sigma$, where $\phi_\sigma$ is the centered normal density with standard deviation $\sigma$. Then
$$\int\frac{(p-q_\sigma)^2}{q_\sigma}\,dx\le\frac49\sigma^4J,\qquad \mathrm{KL}(p\Vert q_\sigma)\le\frac49\sigma^4J,\qquad \int p\left[\log\frac p{q_\sigma}\right]^2dx\le\frac49\sigma^4J.$$

manifest_changes.heading: Statement
manifest_changes.before: If f is C^2 on [a,b] and L is the affine interpolant through (a,f(a)) and (b,f(b)), then |f(x)-L(x)| <= M(x-a)(b-x)/2 for every x in [a,b], where M=max_[a,b]|f''|.
manifest_changes.after:
Let $a<b$ and let $f$ be $C^2$ on an open interval containing $[a,b]$. Put
$M:=\sup_{t\in[a,b]}|f''(t)|$, which is finite, and let $L$ be the unique affine
function with $L(a)=f(a)$ and $L(b)=f(b)$. Then for every $x\in[a,b]$,
$$|f(x)-L(x)|\le \frac{M}{2}(x-a)(b-x).$$

manifest_changes.heading: Statement
manifest_changes.after:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $d,m\ge1$ be finite, fix $T>0$, and work on
the complete usual filtered probability space of
[[def-ito-sde-and-strong-solution]]. Let $0<h\le1$ with $N=T/h\in\mathbb N$.
Use Euclidean state norms and the Frobenius matrix norm. Let $W$ be an adapted
standard $m$-dimensional Brownian motion whose increments are independent of
the current filtration. Let
$b:[0,T]\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$ and
$\sigma:[0,T]\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^{d\times m}$ be jointly Borel,
and suppose finite nonnegative constants $L,K$ satisfy, for all $s,t\in[0,T]$ and
$x,y\in\mathbb R^d$,
$$|b(t,x)-b(t,y)|+\|\sigma(t,x)-\sigma(t,y)\|_F\le L|x-y|,$$
$$|b(t,x)|^2+\|\sigma(t,x)\|_F^2\le K^2(1+|x|^2),$$
and
$$|b(t,x)-b(s,x)|+\|\sigma(t,x)-\sigma(s,x)\|_F \le K(1+|x|)|t-s|^{1/2}.$$
Let $X_0$ be $\mathcal F_0$-measurable, independent of
$\sigma(W_t-W_0:0\le t\le T)$, with $\mathbb E|X_0|^2<\infty$. Let $X$ be the exact continuous
strong solution with
$$\mathbb E\sup_{t\le T}|X_t|^2<\infty,$$
and let $Y^h,\bar Y^h$ be the continuous Euler interpolation and left-endpoint
step process of
[[def-euler-maruyama-step-process-and-continuous-interpolation]]. The
uniform pointwise moment and interpolation-increment bounds of
[[thm-euler-maruyama-uniform-moment-and-increment-bounds]] then imply that a
constant $C$, independent of $h$, satisfies
$$\mathbb E\sup_{0\le t\le T}|X_t-Y_t^h|^2\le Ch.$$
Thus the grid-point root-mean-square error is $O(h^{1/2})$. The constant may
depend on $T,d,m,L,K$ and the exact-solution supremum-moment bound supplied by
the P-SDE-01 existence theorem.

manifest_changes.heading: Statement refuted
manifest_changes.after: If a finite importance sample has weight-based effective sample size $n$, then the sample has visited every region to which the target assigns positive probability.

manifest_changes.heading: Statement
manifest_changes.after:
On $\mathsf X=(0,1]$, let $\lambda$ be Lebesgue probability and
$$P(x,A)=(1-\sqrt{x})1_A(x)+\sqrt{x}\lambda(A).$$
Then $P$ is Lebesgue-irreducible, aperiodic and Harris recurrent, with invariant law $\pi(dx)=dx/(2\sqrt{x})$. It converges from every state, but it is not geometrically ergodic in the standard sense: there are no $r\in(0,1)$ and function $M:\mathsf X\to[0,+\infty]$, finite $\pi$-almost everywhere, such that
$$\lVert P^n(x,\cdot)-\pi\rVert_{\rm TV}\le M(x)r^n\quad(n\ge1)$$
for $\pi$-almost every $x$.

manifest_changes.heading: Statement
manifest_changes.after:
Let $(\mathsf X,\mathcal X)$ be countably generated, let $\mu$ be a nonzero $\sigma$-finite measure, and let $K$ be a probability kernel. There are a jointly measurable $p:\mathsf X\times\mathsf X\to[0,\infty]$ and a subprobability kernel $S$ such that
$$K(x,A)=\int_Ap(x,y)\,\mu(dy)+S(x,A),$$
where $S(x,\cdot)$ and $\mu$ are mutually singular for each $x$.

manifest_changes.heading: Statement
manifest_changes.after:
Let $(\mathsf X,\mathcal X)$ be countably generated, let $P$ be a probability kernel that is $\phi$-irreducible ([[def-phi-irreducible-chain]]), and let $\phi$ be a nonzero $\sigma$-finite irreducibility measure. Then there are an integer $m\ge1$, a measurable $C$ with $\phi(C)>0$, a probability $
u$ with $
u(C)>0$, and $\epsilon>0$ such that $P^m(x,\cdot)\ge\epsilon
u(\cdot)$ for every $x\in C$.

manifest_changes.heading: Example
manifest_changes.before: For U(q)=sqrt(1+q^2) on R and M=1, the target is proper, grad U(q)=q/sqrt(1+q^2) is globally 1-Lipschitz, and the Hamiltonian vector field F(q,p)=(p,-grad U(q)) is globally Lipschitz. The exact flow is complete and obeys the stated Gronwall stability bound.
manifest_changes.after: Take $d=1$, $M=1$, and $U(q)=\sqrt{1+q^2}$. This gives a proper target, a globally $1$-Lipschitz force, and a complete exact Hamiltonian flow with the Gronwall stability estimate from [[thm-exact-hamiltonian-flow-preserves-energy-and-volume]].

manifest_changes.heading: Example
manifest_changes.before: For U(q)=q^2/2, M=1, epsilon=1, L=1, and initial phase point (0,1), leapfrog gives the flipped proposal (1,-1/2). The Hamiltonian rises from 1/2 to 5/8, so the Metropolis acceptance probability is exp(-1/8), strictly less than one.
manifest_changes.after: For the one-dimensional standard-normal potential $U(q)=q^2/2$, unit mass, $\epsilon=1$, one leapfrog step, and initial phase point $(0,1)$, the proposed energy rises by $1/8$ and the Metropolis acceptance probability is $e^{-1/8}$.

manifest_changes.heading: Example
manifest_changes.before: For U(q)=q^2/2, M=1, epsilon=sqrt(2), and L=4, one leapfrog step has matrix A=[[0,sqrt(2)],[-sqrt(2)/2,0]], so A^2=-I and A^4=I. The momentum-flipped proposal leaves q unchanged and has acceptance probability one; starting q=0 therefore remains at zero although the target is N(0,1).
manifest_changes.after: For $U(q)=q^2/2$, $M=1$, $\epsilon=\sqrt2$, and $L=4$, the leapfrog trajectory returns exactly to its initial phase point before the momentum flip. The accepted position therefore never moves; starting at $q=0$ is a trapped state although the standard-normal target assigns positive probability to $[1,2]$.

manifest_changes.heading: Definition
manifest_changes.after:
Use the adaptive MCMC setup of [[def-diminishing-adaptation]]. For
$\epsilon>0$, a state $x\in\mathsf X$, and a fixed parameter $\gamma\in\Gamma$,
define the convergence time
$$M_\epsilon(x,\gamma):=\inf\{m\in\mathbb N:m\ge1,\ \lVert P_\gamma^m(x,\cdot)-\pi\rVert_{\rm TV}\le\epsilon\},$$
with $\inf\varnothing=+\infty$. The power $P_\gamma^m$ is the $m$-fold
composition of the fixed kernel $P_\gamma$; it is not the adaptive transition
law. Assume $M_\epsilon(X_n,\Gamma_n)$ is measurable for each $n$ and
$\epsilon>0$.

For a specified initial probability law $\mu_0$ of $(X_0,\Gamma_0)$, the
adaptive process has **containment** if for every $\epsilon,\delta>0$ there is
an integer $N=N(\epsilon,\delta)$ such that
$$\mathbb P_{\mu_0}\!\left(M_\epsilon(X_n,\Gamma_n)\le N\right)\ge1-\delta\quad\text{for every }n\ge0.$$
A process initialized at the fixed pair $(x_*,\gamma_*)$ is the special case
$\mu_0=\delta_{(x_*,\gamma_*)}$. Thus containment says that
the fixed-kernel convergence times, evaluated at the current state and
parameter, form a sequence bounded in probability under the specified initial
law. It does not assert a uniform deterministic bound for every possible
state and parameter.

manifest_changes.heading: Statement
manifest_changes.after:
Let $(\mathsf X,\mathcal X)$ and $(\Gamma,\mathcal G)$, the jointly
measurable probability-kernel family $(P_\gamma)_{\gamma\in\Gamma}$, common
invariant probability $\pi$, and adaptive process $(X_n,\Gamma_n)$ satisfy
[[def-diminishing-adaptation]]. Fix an initial law $\mu_0$ for
$(X_0,\Gamma_0)$; a fixed initial pair is the Dirac-law special case. If
diminishing adaptation holds under this law and either of the following
conditions holds, then
$$\lVert\mathcal L_{\mu_0}(X_n)-\pi\rVert_{\rm TV}\longrightarrow0.$$

1. **Simultaneous uniform ergodicity:** for every $\epsilon>0$ there is an
   integer $N(\epsilon)\ge1$ such that
   $$\sup_{x\in\mathsf X,\,\gamma\in\Gamma}\lVert P_\gamma^{N(\epsilon)}(x,\cdot)-\pi\rVert_{\rm TV}\le\epsilon.$$

2. **Containment:** for every $\epsilon,\delta>0$ there is an integer $N$
   such that
   $$\mathbb P_{\mu_0}\!\left(M_\epsilon(X_n,\Gamma_n)\le N\right)\ge1-\delta\quad\text{for every }n\ge0,$$
   where $M_\epsilon$ is the fixed-kernel convergence time from
   [[def-adaptive-mcmc-containment]].

The conclusion is convergence of the one-time marginal distributions. It does
not itself assert a strong law, a central limit theorem, or convergence of
sample averages.

manifest_changes.heading: Example
manifest_changes.before: Compare M_0: theta=0 and M_1: theta distributed uniformly on [0,1], each with positive model weight, under Y|theta~Bernoulli(theta). At y=0 both model evidences are positive finite; M_0 has positive posterior probability because it has positive prior model mass, whereas the continuous parameter prior assigns theta=0 probability zero.
manifest_changes.after:
Let $M_0$ have parameter space $\Theta_0=\{0\}$ and prior $\Pi_0=\delta_0$,
and let $M_1$ have parameter space $\Theta_1=[0,1]$ and uniform prior
$\Pi_1=\lambda|_{[0,1]}$. Use the common data space $\mathcal Y=\{0,1\}$ with
counting measure $\mu$, and specify the jointly measurable Bernoulli density
on each parameter space by $f_i(\theta,0)=1-\theta$ and
$f_i(\theta,1)=\theta$. Give the models prior weights $w_0,w_1>0$ with
$w_0+w_1=1$. After observing $y=0$, model $M_0$ has positive posterior
probability because it is an explicit model atom with positive prior weight. A
single continuous prior on $[0,1]$ instead assigns $\theta=0$ probability
zero.
